cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (cross-study combination)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “TOTAL* LDL-C REDUCTIONS o Roszet 10 mg/10 mg 64% o Roszet 20 mg/10 mg 66% o Roszet 40 mg/10 mg 72%” | “Roszet 5 mg/10 mg total LDL-C reduction is 59%.”
cases.context: Asterisk note: '(1-52%)*(1-25%) = 36%' combining rosuvastatin monotherapy study with separate ezetimibe add-on study (different statins, populations, durations).
cases.rationale: Calculated by combining two unrelated studies; no scientific basis.
cases.check: Are efficacy numbers derived by mathematically combining separate studies rather than from a study of the product itself?

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (mITT/LOCF, secondary endpoints, timing)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “Patients Can Get Below 70 mg/dL with One Pill Daily” | “Mean LDL-C Reductions Achieved in Clinical Trials” o “GRAVITY Study Baseline LDL-C 163 mg/dl Final LDL-C 65 mg/dl after 12 weeks (Dose: rosuvastatin/ezetimibe 10 mg/10 mg)” ... o “EXPLORER Study Baseline LDL-C 189 mg/dl Final LDL-C 57 mg/dl after 6 weeks (Dose: rosuvastatin/ezetimibe 40 mg/10 mg)”
cases.context: mITT + LOCF bias; <70 mg/dL was one of many secondary endpoints without multiplicity control; GRAVITY week 12 = 6 weeks monotherapy + 6 weeks combination.
cases.rationale: Study limitations preclude quantitative conclusions; mischaracterizes treatment duration.
cases.check: Are cited study results based on uncontrolled secondary endpoints, biased analysis populations, or mischaracterized treatment durations?

cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “Roszet Delivers Powerful LDL-C Reductions” | “Patients Can Get Below 70 mg/dL with One Pill Daily”
cases.context: Indication is 'as an adjunct to diet'; full indication only in small ISI paragraph at bottom of page one.
cases.rationale: Omits adjunct-to-diet qualifier, implying drug alone provides benefits.
cases.check: Rule: if the label indication includes 'adjunct to diet (and exercise)', benefit headlines must carry that qualifier.

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: Benefit claims in colorful graphics and large bolded headlines with white space; contraindications relegated to bottom of page one and W&P to subsequent page in small paragraph font; only common ARs (e.g., myalgia) shown under “Safety and Tolerability” while myopathy/rhabdomyolysis W&P is on the next page.
cases.rationale: Risk not presented with comparable prominence and readability.
cases.check: Rule: compare font size/position of contraindications and W&P vs benefit headlines; flag if only common ARs appear in the body.
